title: Lionel Messi exits last MLS game before World Cup with apparent injury
content:
Argentina forward Lionel Messi exited Inter Miami’s final MLS game before the World Cup on Sunday with an apparent injury.

Messi walked toward the sideline, asked for a substitute and then immediately left the pitch down the tunnel. He was seen grabbing at the back of his leg. It was the 73rd minute of Miami’s wild match against the Philadelphia Union, which was tied 4-4 at the time. Miami wound up winning 6-4 in the second-highest-scoring game in MLS history, on goals by Luis Suárez (81st minute to complete his hat trick) and Messi’s Argentina teammate Rodrigo De Paul (third minute of stoppage time).

Inter Miami did not provide an official diagnosis after the match, but remarks from interim manager Guillermo Hoyos in his postgame press conference seemed to play down any potential severity.

Fitness pending, Messi is due to join Argentina for World Cup preparations after this match, which was Miami’s last before MLS takes a six-week break. It’s the second straight World Cup preceded by a Messi injury scare, after he suffered from an inflamed Achilles in November 2022 while playing for PSG. He wound up playing every minute for Argentina in its seven matches in Qatar.

Argentina is the defending World Cup champion and drew a group featuring Algeria, Austria and Jordan. The side’s first group game is June 16 against Algeria in Kansas City. Argentina will play two pre-tournament friendlies in college football stadiums in the U.S. on June 6 (vs. Honduras at Texas A&M’s Kyle Field) and June 9 (vs. Iceland at Auburn’s Jordan-Hare Stadium).

Messi, 38, is still viewed as one of the best players in the world and is vital to Argentina’s hopes this summer. He is the back-to-back MLS MVP, the first player in league history to win the award in consecutive years. He has 13 goals and seven assists in 16 matches this year. He has been in his best form of the year heading toward the World Cup, with five goals and seven assists in his last five games, including Sunday.

The global icon has 116 goals in 198 appearances for Argentina.
